findings.patternName: Count-Gated / Winner-Take-All Pot Decoupled From Value Paid
findings.description: The nudge gate is purely numeric — `qualifies = _nudgeSize != 0 && count >= _nudgeSize` (:352) — and the payout is this contract's ENTIRE pre-loop balance of every caller-listed ERC20, sent to a caller-chosen `recipient`. Nothing compares the payout to the value the caller actually contributed. This is the exact H-01/M-01 lineage (BatchNFTMinter value-blind nudge + MEV first-claimer front-run), now RELOCATED into the new multi-token file, and generalised: the reward ASSET is now caller-selected too, so the caller enumerates and sweeps any ERC20 the contract holds.
mitigationsPresent: Pot snapshotted BEFORE the mint loop (`_snapshotRewards`, :416-436) — satisfies notVulnerableWhen 'pot snapshotted BEFORE the loop', which kills the self-funded round-trip variant.
Minter and dispatcherIndex are owner-pinned, so the caller cannot fake `count` with a no-op minter — qualifying requires genuinely paying for >= nudgeSize real mints.
Per-token `minRewards` floor checked pre-pull, so a front-run loser does not pay mint costs.
missingMitigations: Payout is NOT bounded by the contributor's own paid value.
Recipient is NOT pinned to a non-caller address.
findings.exploitableIf: The pot's value exceeds the marginal cost of the `nudgeSize` mints required to qualify. The contract's own NatSpec asserts this can never happen ('the pot is by construction a fraction of the cost of the nudgeSize mints'), but that is a claim about live dispatcher pricing and donation rate, not an enforced invariant — see ledger F-20-07 (WATCH-19), which already records that one of the two premises no longer holds. Over-funding is an owner FOOTGUN (Law 3, in scope); permissionless front-run of a legitimately-funded pot is a valid MEV finding.

findings.patternName: Count-Gated / Winner-Take-All Pot Decoupled From Value Paid
findings.description: SURVIVES VERBATIM. `rewardTokens` is caller-supplied and deliberately NOT deduped (documented at :258-266 and :412-415). Two identical entries snapshot the SAME balance twice, and `_payRewards` then attempts to transfer that snapshot twice. Confirms ledger M-02 is still live, relocated from BatchNFTMinter.sol to BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol.
mitigationsPresent: The code comment claims the second transfer 'fails closed' on insufficient balance.
missingMitigations: No dedupe pass, and the fail-closed claim is conditional, not structural.
findings.exploitableIf: The fail-closed argument only holds when the contract's balance at payout time equals the pre-loop snapshot. It does NOT: the dispatcher donates reward token into this contract on EVERY mint (the design's own stated premise), so at payout time balance == snapshot + thisBatchDonations. The first transfer pays `snapshot`, leaving `thisBatchDonations`; a duplicate second entry succeeds for the full `snapshot` whenever thisBatchDonations >= snapshot — i.e. whenever the batch is large relative to the prior pot. That recaptures the caller's OWN batch donations, which is precisely what the load-bearing 'donate forward' mechanic at :327-344 exists to prevent. A duplicate entry is therefore not merely self-harm to a careless caller; it is a deliberate bypass of the pre-loop snapshot. Also note ledger Q-01: the §6 witness test for §4.5 never configures donations, so the suite certifies the fail-closed property under exactly the conditions where it is trivially true.

findings.patternName: Count-Gated / Winner-Take-All Pot Decoupled From Value Paid
findings.description: SURVIVES VERBATIM. Step 10 reads the contract's ENTIRE payment-token balance and transfers all of it to `msg.sender`, with no nudgeSize gate, no qualification check, and no comparison against what the caller actually pulled in at step 5. Any payment-token balance the contract holds for any reason — accumulated sub-threshold dust from every prior batch, a third-party donation, operational float — leaves with the next caller. Relocated instance of ledger M-01 (BatchNFTMinter step-10 sweep).
mitigationsPresent: The payment token is structurally excluded from `rewardTokens` (:426-428), so it cannot ALSO be claimed via the nudge path.
`count == 0` reverts, so a zero-cost sweep still requires paying for >= 1 mint.
missingMitigations: Refund is not bounded by `paymentAmount - actualSpend`; it is a whole-balance sweep.
findings.exploitableIf: The contract holds any payment-token balance not belonging to the current caller. The cheapest extraction is a 1-mint batch. Note the `totalPaid` return floors at 0 on a net-positive call (:384), which is the arithmetic tell that the sweep can exceed the caller's own contribution.

findings.patternName: Count-Gated / Winner-Take-All Pot Decoupled From Value Paid
findings.description: SURVIVES VERBATIM. The minter is approved for `type(uint256).max` rather than `paymentAmount`, so an under-funded batch does not revert at the funding boundary — it silently spends the contract's own pre-existing payment-token balance to complete the mints. The approval is scoped to the call (revoked at :368) and the minter is owner-pinned and trusted, so this is not a theft-by-minter vector; the issue is that the allowance ceiling is decoupled from the value the caller supplied. Relocated instance of ledger M-07. NOT filed as FRONTRUN-APPROVE (that pattern is skipped as C4 QA and describes a different failure).
mitigationsPresent: Allowance revoked to 0 at :368 within the same call.
Minter is owner-pinned state, not a call parameter.
missingMitigations: No post-loop assertion that spend <= paymentAmount.
findings.exploitableIf: The contract holds a payment-token balance at call time (see PAT-003 — the two compose: an attacker under-funds a batch to spend the residual balance on their own mints, then the step-10 sweep returns whatever is left to them).

findings.location: src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:62 (no ReentrancyGuard) and :238-243 (no nonReentrant); contrast src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:82 and :300
findings.description: CLONE/FORK DRIFT — REALISED. The new `BatchNFTMinterMultiToken` inherits `ReentrancyGuard` (:82) and marks `batchMint` `nonReentrant` (:300), with NatSpec at :78-81 explicitly calling the guard 'required rather than optional'. The deployed sibling `BatchNFTMinter` does NEITHER: `contract BatchNFTMinter is Ownable, Pausable, IPausable` (:62) and `function batchMint(...) external whenNotPaused returns (uint256 totalPaid)` (:243). The mint loop at :286-288 calls `nftMinter.mint(_dispatcherIndex, recipient)` with a CALLER-CHOSEN `recipient`, so `onERC1155Received` fires on attacker-controlled code once per iteration — before the nudge payout (:300-303) and before the dust sweep (:305-311). The hardening was applied to the copy and not to the original: exactly the drift class ledger L-07 escalated from precaution to realised defect.
mitigationsPresent: The pre-loop nudge snapshot (:277-281) means a reentrant call re-reads the SAME pot, and the first payout to complete drains it — so the classic double-pay is blunted by the snapshot ordering rather than by a guard.
The mid-loop window is claimed safe in prior triage (ledger L-01 submitted as Low).
missingMitigations: No contract-wide reentrancy lock; the sibling set (batchMint + the whole-balance sweep at :305) shares payment-token state.
Ledger Q-02 records that NO test exercises this attacker surface at all.
findings.exploitableIf: A reentrant `onERC1155Received` re-enters `batchMint`. The inner call snapshots the nudge pot at the same value as the outer, and the step-10 whole-balance sweep (:305) is reachable by the inner call while the outer call's `paymentAmount` is sitting in the contract — the inner sweep would carry the outer batch's unspent budget out. Combined with PAT-003/PAT-004 this is a value path, not just a guard omission. Prior triage ranked the bare guard omission Low; the drift + the sweep interaction warrants re-examination at the interaction tier rather than auto-reconciling to L-01.

findings.location: src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol:766 (unconditional tail `_recomputeSchedule()`), :512-532 (window restart), consumed by src/InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol:253-300 (migrateIn slices) and src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:189-194
findings.description: STILL LIVE at c881a42 — regression-confirms open ledger M-03/M-04. `_recomputeSchedule()` unconditionally restarts the whole depletion window (`windowEnd = block.timestamp + windowSeconds; lastRewardTime = block.timestamp`, :529-530) and re-spreads the remaining budget across a FRESH full window. `depositFor` calls it on every single re-injection (:766). `InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.migrateIn(start, end)` re-injects users in owner-chosen SLICES across separate transactions, so each slice both restarts the window and begins accruing while later slices are still parked and earning nothing. This is the same Linear-Depletion / rate-drift class as the fixed ledger M-01 (which measured 63.26% mis-allocation to an active staker) and as phlimbo-ea's Linear-Depletion bug.
mitigationsPresent: `_updatePool` caps elapsed at `min(now, windowEnd) - lastRewardTime` (:462), so no retroactive accrual for a period before a staker entered.
Emissions are frozen while the pool is `Migrating`.
missingMitigations: No mechanism holds the window fixed across a multi-slice re-injection.
Parked users accrue nothing while slice-1 users accrue at a rate sized against a budget that is notionally theirs too.
findings.exploitableIf: The operator re-injects in more than one slice/transaction, or any real time elapses between `finalizeAndReset` and the last `migrateIn`. Both are the DESIGNED operating mode (`migrateIn` is explicitly paginated and `parkedUsersRange` exists to drive it), so this needs no attacker — it is an inter-user value transfer driven by operator batching. Note ledger M-03 already frames this as a POSSIBLE INCOMPLETE FIX of M-01; per CLAUDE.md an incomplete fix ranks second only to a regression.
ledgerCrossRef: L-02 (open, finalizeAndReset does not re-arm the window)

findings.location: src/NFTStakerMigrator.sol:214-241 and the line-for-line twin src/InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol:311-338
findings.description: The story-023 forwarding measures value by a `balanceOf` delta across an external call — `captured = rewardToken.balanceOf(address(this)) - pre` (:220) — and attributes 100% of that delta to whichever user the loop is currently on. The delta is NOT sourced; it is inferred. Any reward-token inflow that lands on the migrator during `depositFor` is credited to the current iteration's user regardless of who it belonged to. The authors are aware and installed `require(captured <= owed)` (:221) as a tripwire, correctly documented as a tripwire and not a haircut.
mitigationsPresent: `pre` is snapshotted PER ITERATION, so a standing donation already sitting in the balance is inside `pre` and does not inflate any delta — this correctly defeats the naive donation attack.
`require(captured <= owed)` bounds attribution by the user's own pre-call `pendingReward`, so an over-large foreign inflow reverts rather than being misattributed.
Forward failure is escrowed via try/catch covering BOTH the revert and false-return branches; `claimForwarded()` is permissionless and self-only; `totalUnforwarded` floors `rescueERC20`.
The two migrator copies are genuinely line-for-line identical (verified) — plan decision D-6 held, no drift here.
missingMitigations: An inflow strictly <= `owed` landing mid-call is silently forwarded to the wrong user with no event distinguishing it from a legitimate settlement capture.

The tripwire converts a mis-pointed dispatcher-hook recipient into a HARD REVERT of the whole owner batch, with no per-user skip — a configuration error becomes a batch-wide DoS on `migrate`/`migrateIn`.
findings.exploitableIf: Reward token gains a transfer callback (phUSD has none today — the migrators' own NatSpec says the guard 'pre-closes the hole if the reward token is ever a callback-bearing one'), OR a dispatcher hook's `recipient` is mis-pointed at the migrator. The second is the realistic case and is a Law-3 owner footgun rather than an attack: a competent non-malicious operator would be surprised that a mis-pointed hook bricks the entire migration batch with `Migrator: capture exceeds owed` and no partial-progress path. Ranked medium confidence because the pattern's exploit conditions require a token/config property not present at HEAD; the DoS framing is the live half.
ledgerCrossRef: H-01 (fix-pending, NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor pays the migrator — this IS the compensating fix, so verify completeness rather than re-report the root cause)

manualReview.patternName: Hostile-Token Reentrancy via Caller-Supplied Token Address
manualReview.description: `rewardTokens` are caller-supplied addresses this contract calls twice — `balanceOf` at :429 and `safeTransfer` at :458 — so an attacker-authored 'token' executes arbitrary code inside `batchMint` at two points. Routed to manual review rather than dropped because the mitigation is real but the surface is genuinely attacker-controlled.
manualReview.whyLowConfidence: The call ORDERING defuses the obvious paths: `balanceOf` runs before any funds are pulled and before the max approval; `safeTransfer` runs after the approval is revoked (:368); `nonReentrant` (:300) blocks re-entry into batchMint. Remaining surface is cross-contract observation and reentry into OTHER Phoenix contracts mid-batch (the minter, the staker) while this contract holds the caller's payment budget — not analysable from the pattern tier alone.
manualReview.needs: Interaction-tier (code-scanner) review of what a hostile rewardToken can reach in the rest of the Phoenix suite during the payout pass.

manualReview.description: Three unbounded loops: `count` mints (:363), `rewardTokens.length` snapshot (:424) and payout (:454). Also `NFTStakerMigrator.migrate` over `users` (:174, :189) and `InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.migrateIn` over the slice (:277).
manualReview.whyLowConfidence: Every one is self-DoS — gas is paid by the caller, and the migrator loops are owner-driven with explicit off-chain batching and a `[start, end)` pagination API. This reconciles to ledger L-02 (uncapped count loop, already submitted Low).
manualReview.needs: Reconcile to ledger L-02; no new work expected.

manualReview.patternName: Escrow Accounting vs Actual Balance Desync
manualReview.description: `surplus = balance - totalUnforwarded` (InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator:394, NFTStakerMigrator:272) underflows and reverts if the reward-token balance ever falls below `totalUnforwarded`. `totalUnforwarded` is credited in the false-return branch of the forwarding try/catch, which assumes a `false` return means no tokens moved.
manualReview.whyLowConfidence: Requires a reward token that returns `false` while still transferring — non-standard/weird-ERC20 territory, which the repo's Known Invalid Findings list excludes, and phUSD is standard. Impact if it did occur is a bricked `rescueERC20` for the reward token plus a last-claimant DoS on `claimForwarded`, not theft. Flagged rather than dropped because it is a hard-revert on an escrow path (Law 1: recall beats tidiness).
manualReview.needs: Confirm phUSD's transfer never returns false-with-effect; then close as known-invalid weird-ERC20.

manualReview.description: `if (remaining / DUST_THRESHOLD != 0)` expresses `remaining >= 1e6` via integer division; the `available < minReward` floor at :431 and `count >= _nudgeSize` at :352 are the other boundary comparisons.
manualReview.whyLowConfidence: Marked superficial: all three boundaries are documented and the operators match the stated semantics. The pattern's own note forbids flagging every require()/if(). The DUST_THRESHOLD division is a readability wart, and the sub-threshold residue it strands is already covered by PAT-003 (the next caller sweeps it). Reconciles to ledger Q-04.
manualReview.needs: Drop unless the severity tier wants the readability note in QA.
